cues.text: From Cathedral School to the See of Kraków

Born in 1030 at Szczepanów, near Kraków , Stanislaus studied at the cathedral school of Gniezno and later in Paris before returning to Poland, where he was ordained and became known for his effective preaching and pastoral care.
In 1072, following the death of Bishop Lambert, he was chosen to succeed him as bishop of Kraków.
A Miracle in a Land Dispute

Tradition relates that Stanislaus, having purchased land for the diocese from a nobleman named Piotr, faced a legal challenge after Piotr's death from the man's family, who denied the sale — with King Bolesław II siding against the bishop.

Given three days to produce a witness, Stanislaus, after intense prayer, is said to have gone with witnesses to Piotr's grave and raised him from the dead long enough for the deceased man to testify to the sale's legitimacy.
Confronting the King

Stanislaus's relationship with Bolesław II deteriorated further as the king's conduct grew increasingly tyrannical, including, by tradition, the abduction of a nobleman's wife and brutal punishments inflicted on the wives of soldiers who had deserted a failed campaign.

Later accounts portray Stanislaus as denouncing the king's cruelty and injustice; the precise nature of their conflict, including whether Stanislaus formally excommunicated Bolesław, remains historically disputed.
Martyred at the Altar
When Stanislaus refused to lift the excommunication and halted services rather than let the excommunicated king enter the cathedral, an enraged Bolesław sent guards to kill the bishop.

When they refused to strike, the king, by the traditional account, personally cut Stanislaus down himself while the bishop was celebrating Mass at the Chapel of St. Michael outside Kraków, on 11 April 1079 .
A King's Downfall
The killing of a bishop at the altar shocked Poland and beyond, and Bolesław, having lost the support needed to hold his throne, was forced to flee into exile in Hungary, never to regain his crown.
Stanislaus's relics were transferred to Kraków Cathedral in 1088, and he was formally canonized by Pope Innocent IV in 1253, becoming Poland's first native saint.
Legacy
Stanislaus is venerated as the principal patron of Poland and of the city and Diocese of Kraków.
He is remembered as a symbol of the Church's willingness to hold even the highest secular power accountable to justice and moral law.
Pope John Paul II , himself a former archbishop of Kraków, called Stanislaus the patron saint of moral order.
It was a fitting tribute to a bishop whose opposition to royal authority, according to the traditional account, cost him his life while he celebrated Mass.
